NDT training in Akron, OH: how it works

Short answer: If you live or work around Akron, you can study NDT theory self-paced online on the Atlantis portal, ask an ASNT NDT Level III your questions as you go, and then do the hands-on practical in person at your employer's plant or shop. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Akron. Training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A, so the certificate at the end comes from your employer, not from the course.

Akron built its name on rubber, and the industries that grew from that history still depend on inspection. Tire and polymer companies run test labs and production lines full of steel molds, presses, boilers and heat exchangers. Down the road in Canton and North Canton, bearing and specialty bar steel plants ship product that customers expect to arrive free of seams, laps and internal flaws. Between those anchors sit hundreds of machine shops, forging and casting houses, fabricators and maintenance contractors in Summit, Stark, Portage and Medina counties. Each of them needs someone who can find a defect and write it up properly.

We wrote this page for two groups. One is the person in Northeast Ohio who wants to start an NDT career or add a method and is comparing a college course, an employer program and an online route. The other is the plant or quality manager who has to get technicians qualified and documented without losing them for weeks. The published US course fees appear in the table on this page.

How to get NDT certified in Akron: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

  1. Pick a method that matches local work. Around Akron that is usually magnetic particle or ultrasonic testing for steel parts and welds, penetrant testing for nonmagnetic castings, and visual testing for everything.
  2. Check the entry requirements. Use the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker to see the classroom hours and experience your level and method call for, and confirm your near-vision and color-contrast checks.
  3. Complete the theory. Study the method online at your own pace. Access opens the moment you enrol, so a new hire can start the same week.
  4. Log supervised experience. Your employer records the hours you spend testing under a qualified technician. Under SNT-TC-1A those hours are method hours, not general shop time.
  5. Practise, then sit the practical. Rehearse in the Practical NDT simulator, then perform the practical on real parts at your workplace, examined under a written practice built on SNT-TC-1A.
  6. Pass the general, specific and practical examinations. Your employer's written practice sets the passing grades and who administers each exam.
  7. Receive employer certification. Your employer signs the certification and keeps the records an auditor will ask to see.

If you want a credential that travels with you between Ohio employers, ASNT central certification (ASNT 9712 at Level I and II, or the ASNT NDT Level III examinations) is the other route, and the same study prepares you for it.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Akron technicians

Level 1 technicians perform tests under instruction, Level 2 technicians set up equipment and interpret results against a code or specification, and Level 3 people write procedures and run the program. See Level 1 training, Level 2 training and ASNT Level III preparation for the full outlines.

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Akron
Magnetic particle (MT)Magnetization methods, field direction, wet and dry particles, fluorescent inspection, demagnetizationForgings, bars, bearing components, crane parts, structural welds
Ultrasonic (UT)Sound theory, straight and angle beam, calibration blocks, thickness gauging, flaw sizingBar and billet quality, weld inspection, pressure equipment, corrosion surveys
Penetrant (PT)Cleaning, penetrant types, dwell, developers, interpretation of indicationsAluminum and stainless castings, machined parts, nonmagnetic welds
Visual (VT)Lighting, gauges, weld profile, surface condition, record keepingWeld acceptance, incoming inspection, maintenance shutdowns
Radiography (RT) theoryExposure principles, image quality, film and digital interpretationReviewing images produced by licensed radiography contractors

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Akron

Ultrasonic testing matters more in a steel-making and forging region than almost anywhere else, because internal flaws in a bar or forging cannot be seen from the surface. A UT course teaches you how sound travels through steel, how to calibrate on reference blocks, and how to tell a real reflector from geometry or grain noise. Thickness gauging on vessels, piping and tanks is the other common local use. The ultrasonic testing training page sets out the Level I and II content.

Magnetic particle testing is the companion method for most Akron and Canton plants, since it finds the surface cracks and seams that matter on bearing steel and forged parts. Many technicians here are certified in MT first and add UT within a year or two.

Codes and specifications Akron technicians work to

A Level II technician is judged on whether the test matched the document that governs the part, so it helps to know the documents common in this region before you start. Steel bar and forging producers usually test to ASTM practices, such as the ultrasonic examination standards for forgings and the magnetic particle practice ASTM E1444, combined with acceptance limits written into the customer's purchase order. Pressure equipment and boiler work runs to ASME Section V for the test method and to the construction or repair code for acceptance. Structural and machinery fabricators lean on AWS D1.1 for visual and ultrasonic weld examination.

The practical skill that matters most is reading those documents carefully. A specification may require a particular calibration block, a scanning direction relative to the grain flow, a minimum field strength or a fluorescent rather than visible particle system. Training that only teaches the physics leaves new technicians unsure which instruction applies. The Atlantis courses walk through how a procedure turns a code requirement into steps, and your employer's own procedures then take over on the shop floor.

What hiring managers around Akron tend to look for

Plants and inspection contractors in Summit and Stark counties regularly say the same things about new hires: they want someone who keeps clean records, asks before guessing, and understands why a part is rejected. Classroom hours and a passed general exam open the door, but a candidate who can talk through a calibration, describe an indication accurately and explain which document set the acceptance limit stands out. If you are applying for a trainee role, mention which methods you have studied, how many supervised hours you have logged, and whether you have used the practice tests and simulator to prepare.

Where NDT technicians work around Akron

  • Tire and polymer manufacturing. Goodyear's headquarters in Akron and the wider polymer industry rely on maintenance and quality teams who inspect molds, presses, boilers and plant piping.
  • Bearings and specialty steel. Timken in North Canton and Metallus in Canton produce bearings, power transmission products and alloy steel bar, work that leans on MT and UT.
  • Forging, casting and machining. Independent shops across Summit and Stark counties supply automotive, heavy equipment, oil and gas and defense customers, each with its own inspection specification.
  • Power and utilities. Generating stations and transmission work in Northeast Ohio need weld, boiler and component inspection during outages.
  • Fabrication and construction. Structural steel, pressure vessel and piping fabricators work to AWS and ASME codes and need visual and volumetric inspection.
  • Inspection service companies. Contractors based in the Akron, Canton and Cleveland area send technicians to plants across the state.

NDT schools and classes near Akron: what to compare

There are two broad kinds of training near Akron. College programs give a structured introduction with shared equipment, and they suit someone not yet working in the field. Self-paced theory combined with a practical at the employer suits people already employed and companies that want training tied to their own parts and procedures. Neither is right for everyone.

Whichever you consider, ask the same questions:

  • How many classroom hours does the course give for each method, and do they meet SNT-TC-1A recommendations for your level?
  • Who runs the practical, on what parts, and does it count under your employer's written practice?
  • Who will certify you at the end? A training provider does not certify under SNT-TC-1A; an employer does.
  • Can you reach a Level III with questions while you study?
  • Does the course prepare you for ASNT central examinations if you want them later?

If welding inspection is part of your job, Atlantis also offers a six-day AWS CWI exam-prep course; AWS administers the exam and grants the certification.

Online NDT training in Ohio

Online theory works well across Ohio because so much of the work is shift-based. A technician on rotating shifts in Canton or a quality inspector in Barberton can study in the gaps instead of taking unpaid days off. On the Atlantis portal the material is self-paced, courses run year-round, and an ASNT NDT Level III answers questions in writing. There are no set class times to fit around.

The Ohio NDT training page covers the state as a whole, and nearby city pages for Cleveland, Columbus and Toledo describe those markets. The national overview is on NDT training in the USA.

Training a crew at your Akron facility

For employers, the simplest arrangement is to train people where they already work. Your technicians complete theory online, practise in the simulator, and take the hands-on practical at your facility on the parts they actually inspect, so the examination reflects your products rather than a generic sample set.

A sound program also needs a written practice. If yours is missing, out of date or no longer matches what your customers require, see written practice development. Plants that need an outside Level III to approve procedures and administer examinations can read about Level III consulting. Send us your methods, headcount and customer requirements and we reply within one business day.

Radiography licensing in Ohio

Ohio is an NRC Agreement State, and the Ohio Department of Health licenses the use of radioactive sources for industrial radiography. The licensed company is responsible for its radiographers and assistants meeting the state's training and certification rules.

An RT theory course teaches exposure technique and how to read images; it licenses no one to use a source. Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States. Akron-area plants that need radiography hire a licensed contractor, and RT theory helps the people who review those images.

Practise before your practical exam

Most practical failures come from the basics: a sensitivity check skipped, a scan pattern that misses part of the weld, or an indication measured carelessly. The Practical NDT simulator lets you work complete jobs in your browser before you touch real parts, and the free NDT practice tests show which theory topics need more work.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Akron

Where can I find NDT training near me in Akron?

Colleges in Northeast Ohio offer welding and inspection coursework, and self-paced online theory with a practical at your employer is open to anyone in the Akron area. Atlantis has no physical training location in Akron.

How long does it take to get NDT certified in Akron?

It depends on the method and level. The theory can be finished in a few weeks of steady study, but the supervised experience your employer must log usually takes months for Level II.

How much does NDT training cost?

The published US course fees are in the table on this page. Employers training several people can ask for a quote.

Can I take NDT classes online from Ohio?

Yes. Theory is fully online and self-paced. The practical is done hands-on at an employer's facility or the candidate's workplace.

Which NDT method should I learn first in Akron?

Magnetic particle testing is a common first method in the steel and forging plants around Akron and Canton. Ultrasonic testing usually follows because it opens more inspection roles.

Will my certification carry over if I change employers?

An SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer that issued it. A new employer can recognize your training and experience records and certify you again, often after its own examinations. ASNT central certification travels with you.

Are there NDT jobs in Akron?

Manufacturers, steel producers, utilities and inspection contractors in Summit and Stark counties hire NDT technicians. Search for trainee or Level I roles if you are starting out.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III from Akron?

Yes. Level III preparation is self-paced online; see the Level III page. ASNT administers the Level III examinations.

Where can I read more common questions?

The NDT training FAQ answers the questions candidates and employers ask most, and all Atlantis training is listed on the main training page.
